raw_case_text:
The patient is a 38-year-old HIV + male, well controlled (CD4 count of 213 cells/mm3 with an undetectable viral load) on dolutegravir and emtricitabine-tenofovir, without any prior ocular problems. He presented with a nonulcerative papulonodular hypopigmented rash with lesions scattered along the bilateral upper and lower extremities, trunk, and abdomen [Figure 1]. H and E staining of the cutaneous biopsy showed Leishmaniasis chassis and infantum. Thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly were also noted. The patient immigrated to the US from Nicaragua at the age of 20 and he has remained in the US since his arrival. The patient was treated with intravenous amphotericin B liposome (7 of 9 doses) and then lost to follow-up. He presented a year later with the same papulonodular rash consistent with cutaneous leishmaniasis. He was retreated with amphotericin (14-dose course) and miltefosine for a 28-day course. Two days after stopping miltefosine, he developed progressive left eye redness, pain, and photophobia.
On day 7 of his symptoms, visual acuity declined to count fingers in the affected left eye. Biomicroscopy showed unilateral 3+ conjunctival and ciliary injections, corneal peripheral haze with focal areas of whitening without epithelial loss or ulceration, and 1+ anterior chamber cell [Figure 2]. No vitreoretinal involvement was noted; however, there was a shallow temporal choroidal effusion of the left eye. Anterior chamber paracentesis was performed for polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis for leishmaniasis. No corneal scrapings were performed since the epithelium was intact. Additional infectious workup included HZV aqueous PCR, serum RPR/FTA, QuantiFERON Gold, and serum VZV. All tests were found to be noncontributory. HIV monitoring laboratories revealed a rise in the HIV viral load to 10,500 copies/mL and a decline in CD4 count to 213 cells/mm3. No changes in medications or compliance were noted at that time.
Cautious initiation of topical steroid (prednisolone acetate 1%) every 2 h and cycloplegic (cyclopentolate 1%) three times per day was done under close monitoring and with the plan to change to topical amphotericin if any worsening occurred. The patient responded rapidly to the application of topical steroids with complete clearing of corneal infiltration and resolution of anterior uveitis [Figure 3]. The visual acuity returned to 20/20 by the Snellen chart. Ocular quiescence has remained off steroids for 2 years even though concurrent cutaneous and visceral disease did recur.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old HIV-positive male presented with progressive left eye redness, ocular pain, photophobia, and vision loss to counting fingers two days after completing miltefosine and liposomal amphotericin B therapy for recurrent cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially presented with a nonulcerative papulonodular hypopigmented rash across the bilateral extremities, trunk, and abdomen accompanied by splenomegaly and thrombocytopenia, received 7 of 9 planned doses of IV liposomal amphotericin B before being lost to follow-up, and returned 1 year later with recurrent cutaneous lesions. He was retreated with a 14-dose course of liposomal amphotericin B and a 28-day course of oral miltefosine; two days after stopping miltefosine, he developed progressive left eye redness, pain, and photophobia, with visual acuity declining to counting fingers by day 7.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV-positive (previously well controlled with undetectable viral load and CD4 count of 213 cells/mm3), history of cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis; immigrated to the United States from Nicaragua at age 20 with no subsequent travel outside the US; no prior ocular history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Home medications include dolutegravir and emtricitabine-tenofovir.

objective.physical_examination: Initial systemic exam showed scattered nonulcerative papulonodular hypopigmented skin lesions on the bilateral upper and lower extremities, trunk, and abdomen, along with splenomegaly. Ophthalmic examination on day 7 of ocular symptoms showed left eye visual acuity of counting fingers, unilateral 3+ conjunctival and ciliary injection, peripheral corneal haze with focal whitening and intact epithelium without ulceration, 1+ anterior chamber cells, no vitreoretinal involvement, and a shallow temporal choroidal effusion.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline workup noted thrombocytopenia; at ocular presentation, serum RPR/FTA, QuantiFERON-TB Gold, and serum VZV were noncontributory.
objective.advanced_workup: Prior skin biopsy (H&E) demonstrated Leishmania chagasi/infantum. At ocular presentation, HIV viral load rose to 10,500 copies/mL with a CD4 count of 213 cells/mm3; anterior chamber paracentesis aqueous PCR for Leishmania and HZV was noncontributory.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Prior cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis (Leishmania chagasi/infantum) had been confirmed on skin biopsy and treated with liposomal amphotericin B and miltefosine; infectious uveitis/keratitis differentials (syphilis, tuberculosis, VZV/HZV, and active intraocular Leishmania replication) were ruled out by negative aqueous PCR and serologies, supporting post-treatment immune-mediated/miltefosine-associated kerato-uveitis. The patient was treated with topical prednisolone acetate 1% every 2 hours and cyclopentolate 1% three times daily under close observation, achieving rapid and complete resolution of corneal infiltration and anterior uveitis with recovery of 20/20 visual acuity and 2-year ocular quiescence off steroids despite subsequent systemic leishmaniasis recurrence.
